description: Wire all four dashboard pages and DashboardTopbar to real API data. Depends on FEAT-001 (app/lib/api/dashboard.ts must exist first). Removes all MOCK_* imports from the four pages and DashboardTopbar. Adds auth gates. Adds loading and error states.
steps: STEP 1 — app/dashboard/overview/page.tsx: This is currently a server async component using `connection()` from next/server and `export const instant = false`. It CANNOT use useAuth() (client hook). Auth gate for server components works by checking cookies/tokens server-side — but since tokens are stored in localStorage, we cannot read them server-side. Decision: Convert overview/page.tsx to a client component ('use client') and use the same pattern as reservations/page.tsx. Remove `connection()` and `export const instant = false`. Add useAuth() + useRouter() for the auth gate. Add useState for data, loading, error. Fetch: call getMyHotel() on mount; if null/error show error state. With hotelId, call getDashboardStats(hotelId), getDashboardReservations(hotelId), getDashboardRoomTypes(hotelId) in parallel using Promise.all. Replace all MOCK_* references with real API data: hotel name in greeting -> hotel.name, stats from getDashboardStats, upcoming reservations from filtered getDashboardReservations, room availability from getDashboardRoomTypes. Remove import of MOCK_HOTEL, MOCK_RESERVATIONS, MOCK_REVENUE_DAYS, MOCK_ROOM_TYPES from '../mock/data'. The revenue chart: if no revenue endpoint exists, compute from reservations (sum amountNgn grouped by checkOut date for the last 7 days) or hide the chart with a 'Revenue data not yet available' placeholder — choose the placeholder approach since the bar chart relies on MOCK_REVENUE_DAYS which has no API equivalent in scope.

STEP 2 — app/dashboard/reservations/page.tsx: Already 'use client'. Add useAuth() + useRouter() auth gate at top of component. Remove import of MOCK_RESERVATIONS. Add useState: reservations (DashboardReservation[]), isLoading (boolean), error (string|null). Add useEffect: call getMyHotel() then getDashboardReservations(hotelId). Replace MOCK_RESERVATIONS with the reservations state variable throughout (filtered, totalPages, etc). Show a full-page loading state while isLoading. Show an error banner if error is set. The total count badge changes from MOCK_RESERVATIONS.length to reservations.length. All filter/search/pagination logic stays identical — it operates on the in-memory array.

STEP 3 — app/dashboard/rooms/page.tsx: Currently a plain server component (no 'use client'). Convert to a client component. Remove import of MOCK_ROOM_TYPES. Add useAuth(), useRouter(), useState, useEffect. Auth gate. Fetch getMyHotel() then getDashboardRoomTypes(hotelId). Show loading skeleton (simple spinner or skeleton cards). Replace MOCK_ROOM_TYPES.map(...) with roomTypes.map(...) where roomTypes is the state variable. DashboardRoomType matches RoomType structure exactly (same field names), so no mapping needed in the JSX.

STEP 4 — app/dashboard/inventory/page.tsx: Already 'use client'. Add useAuth() + useRouter() auth gate. Remove import of MOCK_INVENTORY. Change the initial useState from MOCK_INVENTORY to []. Add useEffect: call getMyHotel() then getDashboardInventory(hotelId). Replace MOCK_INVENTORY with the loaded data. The existing edit-cell and save logic stays identical — it operates on local state. Add isLoading and error states. Show loading skeleton when isLoading. If the inventory endpoint returns empty (backend 404 graceful fallback), show a 'No inventory data' message.

STEP 5 — app/dashboard/components/DashboardTopbar.tsx: Currently uses MOCK_HOTEL.name for the hotel name chip and avatar initials. Add useAuth() to get the authenticated user. Replace MOCK_HOTEL.name chip with `{user?.firstName} {user?.lastName}` or simply the user's first name. Replace initials from hotel name with initials from user name: `(user?.firstName?.[0] ?? '') + (user?.lastName?.[0] ?? '')`. Remove import of MOCK_HOTEL from '../mock/data'. Since the topbar only needs the user object (not hotelId), no API call is needed — useAuth() provides it directly.

STEP 6 — Auth gate pattern (same across all four pages): At the top of each client component after the hooks section: `const { user, isLoading: authLoading } = useAuth(); const router = useRouter(); useEffect(() => { if (!authLoading && !user) { router.replace('/auth/signin'); } }, [authLoading, user, router]);` — and early return `if (authLoading) return <LoadingSpinner />` while auth is resolving. This prevents the page from making API calls before auth is confirmed.

STEP 7 — Loading and error UI: Add a simple reusable inline loader. Do not create a new shared component — inline a `
` with a centered spinner SVG or text 'Loading…' styled with --db-* tokens. For errors, show: `

Failed to load data. Please try again.

`.

All 4 pages redirect to /auth/signin when user is not authenticated
Overview page renders hotel name from API user or hotel object, not from MOCK_HOTEL
Reservations page renders real bookings from getDashboardReservations; search and filter work on live data
Rooms page renders real room types from getDashboardRoomTypes
Inventory page renders real inventory from getDashboardInventory (or empty state if backend returns none)
DashboardTopbar shows authenticated user's name/initials, not MOCK_HOTEL.name
StatusBadge still works — normalized BookingStatus values (lowercase) are passed to it
